To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incorporation of radioiodinated long-chain fatty acid analogues into phospholipid fractions of normoxic cardiac tissue is highly dependent on the fatty acid analogue and the type of phospholipids, and that the radioiodinated long chain fatty acid analogues are incorporated into phospholiplid fractions in different patterns, which are only partly comparable with the distribution of their natural counterparts.
the incorporation of IHDA into phospholipid is similar to that of natural fatty acids, while the incorporation of DMIPPA and p-IPP are very different.
The radioiodinated fatty-acids, IHDA, p-IPPA and DMIPPA, have entirely different patterns for incorporation into phospholipopids of canine myocardium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of radioiodinated analogues of fatty acids for the in vivo study of myocardial metabolism and function.
the development of new radioiodinated fatty-acid analogues for the noninvasive detection of cardiac ischemia.
the incorporation of fatty acids into phospholipid fractions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phospholipide incorporation of the three analogues is not similar to the phospholipase A _{2} -induced phospholipid turnover.
IHDA, p-IPPA and DMIPPA are not good substitutes for the natural fatty acids, since they are not incorporated into the phospholippids according to the natural pattern.

the incorporation of radioiodinated long-chain fatty acids into myocardial phospholipids is not only influenced by the fatty acid analogue, but also by the fatty acid composition and the phospholipopid pattern of myocardial membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radioiodinated analogues of IHDA and p—IPPA are useful tools to assess the phospho-lipid distribution of these fatty acids under physiological conditions.
the incorporation of radioiodinated analogues into the myocardial phospholipids is dependent on the structure of the radioiodinatetd fatty acids.

the radioiodinated analogues have different incorporation patterns into the phospholigids.
